@reacher posted the YouTube link on /v/gaming, and there are no direct tabletop applications yet (that I know of) but it's exciting to think of the possibilities. I can see this gaining more traction more quickly in games such as Warhammer and CCGs (Yu-Gi-Oh! has already been mentioned in the YouTube comments).

I know there are some programs to play P&P games online, such as SyncRPG or Roll20, but this would take it to the another level. However, the hazard I see is that imagination can easily outstrip technology in capabilities. We're only just now getting to the point where graphics in actual gameplay are lifelike, and often our P&P games take place in such fanciful worlds that trying to immerse yourself like this couldn't do it justice. On the flip side, once somebody creates the art for it then all you'd need is a world creator and you'd be in business. Exciting times indeed.

I'm a recent transplant from Reddit and absolutely love the r/eagles community over there, so I'm hoping to help generate the content necessary to bring that community this-a-ways. Today I’d like to see what everyone is expecting as our Week 1 starting offense by position. There’s obviously a lot of volatility, especially with the recent departure of Mathis, so I’m curious as to how similar or different these lists turn out.

QB: Sam Bradford. After a preseason filled with half opened eyes and shortness of breath induced by a DE getting close to Sam, he trots out of the tunnel as our Day 1 starter.

RB: Demarco Murray. One of the easiest to predict, I’ll throw in a bonus prediction for fun – Ryan Mathews ends up with more TDs (total) than Murray this year.

WRs: Cooper, Matthews, Agholor. I think Nelson impresses this preseason to the point where he moves into the spot vacated by Maclin on week 1, leaving Matthews in the slot and Cooper keeping Miles Austin's spot warm (I don’t know why, but I have a sneaky feeling Cooper loses out to Austin at some point. Probably insane).

FB: Heath Evans. Just kidding, no one because we’re a soft team.

LT: Jason Peters. Bodyguard. Nuff said.

LG: Matt Tobin. This doesn’t give me the warm and fuzzies, but I honestly aren’t that scared of moving from Mathis, who has truly been one of the game’s best LGs over the last few years, to any sack of bones as long as that sack is between Peters and Kelce. Speaking of which…

C: Jason Kelce. Beard. Nuff said.

RG: Allen Barbre. The praise coming out of camp so far around Barbre doesn’t feel like typical coach/teammate speak. Those at the Novacare seem genuinely impressed by Barbre, so I get the feeling he cements his starting role in the preseason.

RT: Lane Johnson. Better be clean this year. Nuff said.

Bonus prediction: at the end of the season, barring injuries (the caveat for every NFL team), we will have run the ball considerably more than we have passed it, and our time of possession will be top 5 in the NFL despite our pace.

Orange Loaf Cake.

Preparation Time ~ 20 minutes Cooking time ~ 1 hour

INGREDIENTS

120g (1/2 cup) butter, softened
250g (1 cup) caster (superfine) sugar
3 eggs, beaten
Zest and juice of one orange
250g (1 cup) plain flour
1 table spoon baking powder
Juice of 1 orange (yes, we need one more)
3-4 tablespoons of honey
1 orange sliced into rounds and baked on a rack at 250F for 2 hours (could drop it to 1 hour)

PREPARATION

-Preheat the oven to 350F. Grease and line a 1 liter loaf tin.
-Cream the butter and sugar together until pale and creamy, add beaten eggs a bit at a time, beating thoroughly each time.
-Put in zest, juice of one orange, and baking powder. Beat together. Pour into the loaf tin.
-Bake for 50-60 minutes.
-Turn out of the tin (could put it on a wire rack or something at this point).
-Mix the juice of one orange and honey. Pierce the cake with a skewer a couple of times and drizzle with syrup over. Leave to soak for a little bit.
-Decorate with dried orange slices.

All done!

This is one of my favourite cake recipes. Hope you like it, let me know if anyone ends up making it.
